Issue No. 651 Dolly Parton, Teacher Jídé Salawu Dolly Parton, Teacher by Jídé Salawu If you were a child of the early 1990s growing up in Kwara State, north central Nigeria, you had the rare privilege of making radio part of your life. item.title: Older Americans are sliding into poverty
item.description:
The supplemental poverty rate for older Americans has increased. Willowpix/Getty Images After a surge of pandemic-era aid, older Americans have faced rising poverty. Healthcare costs drive older Americans into poverty, straining their savings and finances. Social Security often isn't enough to cover costs, leading older Americans to take on low-paying jobs. After a slew of pandemic-induced aid ran its course, older Americans are falling back into poverty — and even younger would-be retirees are struggling. After the Great Recession, the trendline for older Americans had been improving, and 2020 pandemic relief measures helped buttress the aging population from falling into poverty in the wake of Covid. item.title: Resident Evil Is a Deeply Unhinged Send-Up of Video Games
item.description:
Finally, a movie for people who love shooter video games but are terrible at aiming. Of the many running gags in the new Resident Evil , the one that amused me the most was the protagonist's frustration with guns. The character, a medical courier named Bryan, first discovers a pistol, and then a shotgun, and then eventually heavier weaponry, in an escalating power progression that mirrors the common gaming trope. He has to root through drawers for bullets and food, maneuver conveniently placed ladders, shoot a maddening number of padlocked gates, and defend himself against all manner of creepy-crawly monsters. And all throughout, he struggles with his aim, firing just a few inches from the target even at close range, and occasionally firing stupidly and accidentally, for no reason at all.
